images.title: Rice into equal bags
images.purpose: Show 84 kg and 108 kg of rice packed into equal 12 kg bags, 7 from one farm and 9 from the other.
images.composition: Two rows, one per farm, read left to right: a big heap labelled with its weight, an arrow, then a row of small equal bags; white space between rows.
exact_structure: Row 1: one large teal (#0072B2) rice heap labelled 84 kg, a grey (#6B7280) arrow, then exactly 7 small identical teal (#0072B2) bags in a row, with 7 bags written after them.
Row 2: one large amber (#E69F00) rice heap labelled 108 kg, a grey (#6B7280) arrow, then exactly 9 small identical amber (#E69F00) bags in a row, with 9 bags written after them.
All 16 small bags are the same size; the first bag in row 1 carries a reddish purple (#CC79A7) tag reading 12 kg each.
Below both rows, one caption: HCF of 84 and 108 = 12.
rejection: any number of bags other than 7 in row 1 and 9 in row 2
bags of different sizes, or a bag mixing both colours
any bag weight other than 12 kg
images.takeaway: The heaviest equal bag that suits both farms is the HCF, 12 kg, giving the fewest bags, 7 + 9 = 16.
images.description: 84 kg of rice packed into 7 teal bags and 108 kg into 9 amber bags, every bag 12 kg.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count the bags in each row and check 7 × 12 = 84 and 9 × 12 = 108.

image_decisions.why: The packing story becomes clear when students see the equal bags from each farm.
